plan.title: Lung treated vs control DE with confounded-batch caveat
plan.analytical_narrative: 12 lung samples (6 treated / 6 control) quantified by salmon give a 12000-gene raw count matrix. The metadata shows batch B1 = all controls and B2 = all treated: the batch is perfectly confounded with condition, so no statistical method can separate a batch effect from a treatment effect in this dataset. Per the confounded-design rule (R-0005), the plan does not fit a batch term, does not run ComBat-seq/removeBatchEffect/SVA, and does not claim to 'correct for batch' — any such correction would remove the condition signal along with the batch signal, or vice versa, and give a false sense of validity. Instead: (1) QC first, to show explicitly how batch and condition co-vary in PCA/sample-distance space, so the confound is visible before any test runs and is not hidden by the analysis; (2) a standard DESeq2 Wald test with design ~condition, apeglm-shrunken fold changes, BH-adjusted p-values with independent filtering — every downstream gene called 'differential' is explicitly reported as 'differential between B2-treated and B1-control, batch effect and treatment effect not separable'; (3) an edgeR quasi-likelihood run as a second method, reporting the intersection with DESeq2 as the higher-confidence (but still confounded) set; (4) fgsea preranked GSEA on the Wald statistic against Hallmark, then Reactome and WikiPathways, all carrying the same confounded-result caveat; (5) a report step that states the confound explicitly in every results table and figure, states package versions and thresholds, and does not overclaim causality. This design cannot support a causal claim about 'treatment effect' as distinct from 'processing batch effect' — the plan makes that limitation the headline finding alongside the gene list, not a footnote.

keep genes with >=10 counts in >= smallest group size (6)
design = ~condition (no batch term, batch perfectly confounded); DESeq2 Wald test, apeglm shrinkage
